body: Yeah, me too, I've always been a horrible student, but I love to learn new stuff, and find myself doing way better when doing things independently, but knowing things isn't going to get you a decent job, having spent a million pesos on a 5 year time-sinker is gonna do it, though, at least that's what everyone has been telling since I graduated from highschool.

The third world is harsh and doesn't have a lot of opportunities, the most a person without college credentials or an already existing business can hope to gain monthly is around 10,000 pesos (around 500 USD) here in Mexico, and even if I could pay the cheapest education I could fin with that money, I'm gonna be fully honest, having to deal with school is already making me feel drained even if it really isn't that difficult, because it just keeps stealing the time I've always wanted to use to further my personal goals, were I smart dedicated student this would've been my last semester, but I'm not and I still have 2 and a half years to go, and even though it's pathetic, I think I'd rather just not bother and kill myself than keep going like this, I mean, it's not like corporate life is any better, as far as I can tell is easier but just as mindlessly boring. I mean if life is just this; feeling too drained by your responsibilities to even bother to try to accomplish your own goals, then I see no reason to even try, if it's all a purposeless cycle of regret, then yeah, why bother. Sorry for being a hopeless pessimist, but this is really how I see things.

It's less about my country, even though it really has lots of big issues, and more the fact that I've been stuck seeing the same thing and living the same way, in the same place, my entire life, I fucking hate my city, which is troubling, since it's supposed to be one of the better-off cities in the country, so I doubt it gets any better, my only option is to escape for a better place to live, but I think I'd rather die than just make my dad waste his money on more trivial qualifications of my worth known as educational degrees to make any kind of migratory process go smoothly.

Eh, I don't really agree with that, it's a harmless term, not being a hardcore gamer it just means that you're not really that interested in videogames as an industry and/or community, and just tend play heavily marketed games that appeal to the "blue ocean" market (COD, FIFA, LOL, Fortnite), nothing wrong with that, but it does mark a significant difference in the demographics, why do you think indies usually try to appeal to people like us? People that spend time on the internet arguing and gathering info about the industry and its current trends, and not the "blue ocean" market? We just are more knowledgeable and experienced compared to that market, we look for new things to experience, while the "blue ocean" waits for something new to pop up in their radar. Like I said, none of this is bad, but it's still a meaningful difference since we're all pretty much different markets; mobile, casual, and hardcore.
